sections.heading: The new law, exactly
sections.intro: The requirement is federal law (Public Law 119-21, § 71119) and it is already written into California statute (Welfare and Institutions Code § 14005.69, as amended by AB 2161). Both texts are linked below.

sections.heading: Who is never subject (specified excluded individuals)
sections.intro: These are statutory categories, not a finding about this person. A work-rule exception does not by itself prove an exception from six-month financial eligibility checks; check the separate DHCS eligibility timeline and exceptions. DHCS timeline.

sections.heading: How to comply in a month
sections.intro: These are alternative ways to satisfy the rule; combination is allowed where provided by statute. Seasonal averaging is limited to seasonal workers. None is certified for this person.

sections.heading: Short-term hardship exceptions (state option)
sections.intro: California enacted all four hardship categories in WIC § 14005.69(h). The third one is county-specific: DHCS sends a separate notice if your county qualifies.

sections.heading: What happens if you do not comply
California's implementation — the documents that govern
sections.intro: County eligibility workers work from these. The member-facing letter is the plain-language version of the same rules.

sections.heading: California's one extension of the federal rule
sections.note: California §14005.69(b)(1)(B) also addresses certain state-funded adult coverage. The subject reports U.S. citizenship; immigration/five-year-bar status must not be inferred from this general provision. Enacted statute.

sections.heading: Still not settled by the agencies
sections.intro: DHCS flags these as pending in its own policy letter. Details are on the Flagged for Review page.
